job.style: a description of a classroom activity or experiment and what it shows

response.passage: In our class today, we conducted a 'Digital Safety Workshop' to understand how scammers operate. We learned that fraudsters often use high-pressure tactics, such as claiming your bank account will be closed immediately if you do not click a link to update your KYC. This is a lie; banks never threaten customers with instant account closure via SMS. We also discussed the 'Digital Arrest' scam, where criminals pretend to be police officers on video calls to demand money. Remember, no law enforcement agency has the authority to arrest anyone over a video call or demand payments to avoid jail. Furthermore, we explored the 'Secret Deal' trap. Scammers often ask you to keep an investment opportunity hidden from your family, claiming it is a special chance. This secrecy is a major red flag designed to prevent you from getting advice. Finally, we learned about UPI safety. You only need to enter your PIN when you are sending money, never when you are receiving it. If someone asks you to enter your PIN to get a refund, they are trying to steal your funds. Always report such incidents to the cybercrime portal immediately, as acting quickly increases the chances of recovering your lost money.
response.summary: This workshop taught us to identify common digital scams like fake KYC alerts, digital arrest threats, and secret investment traps. It emphasized that legitimate authorities never demand money or secrecy, and that PINs are only for sending payments.
